subject: inputs/FOUNDER-THESIS-2026-09-13-agents.md
round: F2 — agents / work layer rethink, Step 0
status: frozen input to Step 1; no claim is decided

fixture_shorthand.F1 unknown job: A kind of job nobody anticipated appears mid-build.
fixture_shorthand.F2 demand 4x: Matched scope at 1x, 2x and 4x demand with offer and supplier changes.
fixture_shorthand.F3 three permissions: One task needing three distinct tool permissions.
fixture_shorthand.F4 independent verification: A verification the producer must not influence.
fixture_shorthand.F5 capacity reset: A handoff across a capacity reset.
fixture_shorthand.F6 founder absent: The founder absent for a week.

claims.statement: Splitting one unit of work across N executors creates N-1 responsibility transfers, and a material fraction of transfers lose at least one fact the receiver needed.
claims.measure: Facts lost per handoff, by recall probe: seed each work order with fixed load-bearing facts (an exclusion, a deadline, a promised remedy, a rejected alternative, a unit) and require the receiver to restate each before acting; baseline is the same fixture run in one context with no transfer.
claims.existing_evidence: research/L04-engineering.md (Anthropic Nov-2025 harness experiment: premature completion, oversized attempts, broken handovers despite compaction); research/L03-architectures.md (MAST: 14 failure modes over 1,600+ traces incl. inter-agent misalignment); planning/specification/05-work-agents-skills.md section 5 ('each transformation records losses') concedes the mechanism without measuring it
claims.model_generation_note: Compaction and long-context handling are model-version properties; L04 records one harness intervention becoming unnecessary after a model change.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F5 capacity reset

claims.statement: Under the same fixture and the same accepted outcome, ephemeral-agent-per-task consumes more scarce provider capacity than a single longer context.
claims.measure: Scarce capacity per ACCEPTED outcome in the separated units of 07-integrations-capacity.md section 6 (native job launches, provider quota buckets, wall-clock occupancy), with rework, rejected attempts and abandoned outputs in the denominator per 05 section 6. Never dollars per token.
claims.existing_evidence: research/L04-engineering.md records a showcased comparison of $200 over six hours versus $9 over twenty minutes for a planner/generator/evaluator arrangement, and in the same paragraph states the competing interpretation that some of the difference came from extra computation and richer specifications rather than agent separation
claims.model_generation_note: Per-call capability sets how many calls an outcome needs; L04 records the scaffolding that justified the cost being ablated as the model improved.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F2 demand 4x

claims.statement: Under the same fixture, ephemeral-agent-per-task has higher elapsed time to accepted outcome than a single longer context, after accounting for whatever parallelism the split enables.
claims.measure: Elapsed wall-clock from admission to independent acceptance, median and p95, reported beside the count of executors run concurrently; a latency figure without the concurrency count is uninterpretable.
claims.existing_evidence: research/L04-engineering.md, same six-hours-versus-twenty-minutes case and same competing interpretation; planning/specification/05-work-agents-skills.md section 5 states the elapsed-time trade-off as design and measures neither side
claims.model_generation_note: Faster models shrink the per-step cost the split was buying back.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F2 demand 4x

claims.statement: Facts available in a single context are lost when the same work is split, at a rate higher than the rate at which the single context simply fails to use them.
claims.measure: Two rates on one fixture: facts ABSENT from the executor's context (recall probe) and facts PRESENT AND NOT USED (decision probe: change one load-bearing fact and see whether the output changes). The second is the control that makes the first meaningful.
claims.existing_evidence: research/L05-memory.md (LongMemEval: retrieval success does not guarantee correct use, and isolated-fact extraction harmed overall performance through information loss; Lost in the Middle: position sensitivity; Memora: recurring invalid-memory reuse across four models and six memory agents); research/L04-engineering.md (broken handovers despite compaction)
claims.model_generation_note: Every cited result carries its lane's warning that it does not establish present-model failure rates.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F5 capacity reset, run in both the split and single-context arms

claims.statement: Holding context quality and shared state fixed, varying the number of agents changes accepted outcomes less than holding agent count fixed and varying context quality.
claims.measure: A 2x2 on one fixture set: {few agents, many agents} x {strong shared state, weak shared state}; accepted-outcome rate, capacity per accepted outcome and owner minutes reported separately. The claim survives if the context main effect exceeds the agent-count main effect on accepted outcomes.
claims.existing_evidence: none in package. research/cross-lane-comparison.json X03 records coordination as 'foundational alternatives retained'; planning/02-architecture-selection.md section 1 states the evidence does not establish which candidate runs a business most effectively
claims.model_generation_note: A model that uses long context reliably would weaken the agent-count effect and strengthen the context effect, but nothing in the package establishes the direction.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F1 unknown job, run under both shared-state arms

claims.statement: Parallel work, distinct tools or permissions, isolated context, specialized knowledge and independent verification are jointly sufficient and individually necessary as reasons to create a separate executor.
claims.measure: Adversarial counterexample search in both directions: (a) a real work item needing a separate executor for a reason not on the list (candidates: jurisdictional separation, blast-radius containment, provider or account separation, capacity reservation, legal or professional standing); (b) a listed reason that, alone, yields no measured benefit over one executor. One confirmed instance either way falsifies it.
claims.existing_evidence: none in package as a gate; planning/specification/05-work-agents-skills.md section 4 states a narrower and differently worded gate - 'a demonstrated task distinction, confidentiality boundary, real professional requirement or measured cost/quality benefit'
claims.model_generation_note: A claim about the structure of the list, not about model performance.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F3 three permissions

claims.statement: Where two parts of one job are genuinely independent, running them as separate executors delivers the accepted outcome sooner than running them in one context, by more than the integration cost.
claims.measure: Elapsed time to accepted COMBINED outcome, with integration and merge work charged to the parallel arm, on both a known-independent split and a known-semantic-conflict split. A design that wins the first and loses the second has not won.
claims.existing_evidence: research/L04-engineering.md (METR early-2025 randomized study: experienced maintainers took 19% longer with AI tools on their own repositories; 2026 update calls later estimates unreliable partly because concurrent-agent work is hard to measure); research/L03-architectures.md (ADK read as: decomposition may reduce context pressure but introduce information-loss and coordination boundaries); 05 section 6 ('a clean textual merge is not behavioral compatibility')
claims.model_generation_note: The serial arm's speed is a model property; the integration cost mostly is not.
claims.discriminating_fixture: New - two branches, one product meaning: two executors change onboarding and pricing without touching the same file and the combined journey promises something neither branch promised (conformance case 2, 05 section 9)

claims.statement: Where two parts of one job require different permissions, giving them to one executor increases realised blast radius relative to splitting them, even when the executor is instructed to use each permission only for its own part.
claims.measure: Under an injected prompt-injection or confused-deputy attack on a three-permission fixture, count operations RELEASED outside the part that needed them; one executor holding the union versus three each holding one. Released operations, not attempted ones.
claims.existing_evidence: Decided but unmeasured: planning/02-architecture-selection.md section 4 (C04 sole control of consequences, attenuated authority for private decomposition); 05 section 1 (no workflow, skill, model or worker acquires authority by containing instructions to do so); research/L04-engineering.md ('sandbox enabled' cannot serve as a system-wide safety verdict)
claims.model_generation_note: A permission boundary holds or does not, independently of the capability inside it.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F3 three permissions

claims.statement: Where one part of a job must not see material another part holds, isolation implemented as a separate executor prevents disclosure that a permission-filtered single context does not.
claims.measure: Disclosure count on a seeded fixture: plant a marked private term reachable by part A and check for it in part B's outputs, outward search queries, tool stdout and provider-bound traffic; filtered single context versus separated executors. Count every disclosure destination per 06 section 2.
claims.existing_evidence: 06-knowledge-evidence-evaluation.md sections 2 and 4 specify the filtered-loader alternative in detail, including that narrowing today's tools cannot remove yesterday's data; whether it matches executor separation is untested
claims.model_generation_note: A model that leaks less from held context narrows the gap; 'hidden resumed context' is already a named conformance case in 06 section 9.
claims.discriminating_fixture: New - a private term in an outward query (the adverse variation listed in 06 section 9), run once with isolation by executor and once with isolation by loader filter

claims.statement: For work needing domain competence, a dedicated specialist executor produces better accepted outcomes than a general executor loading a tested domain skill.
claims.measure: Accepted-outcome rate and reviewer-found defect rate on matched domain fixtures, general+skill versus specialist, with selection overhead charged to the general arm and maintenance cost charged to both. 06 section 6 already prescribes the comparison: 'compare a direct procedure with the same outcome criteria'.
claims.existing_evidence: Against: 05 section 4 ('A general model can use a domain skill when the needed competence has passed relevant tests'); repository CLAUDE.md, quoted at HANDOFF-F2 section 2 - 21 named roles collapsed to seven generic engines on the principle that domain expertise is a lens, not an agent (one harness, not a law). For: research/L03-architectures.md records MetaGPT's reported gains from encoded role SOPs while noting its assembly-line assumption
claims.model_generation_note: The general arm's unaided competence is what improves between generations; the skill closes the remaining gap.
claims.discriminating_fixture: New - the stale borrowed skill (conformance case 6, 05 section 9): a skill passes shape checks but its example omits a cancellation duty; specialist and general+skill fail differently and that difference is the measurement

claims.statement: A verifier that is a separate executor detects defects a producer's own self-check misses, at a rate high enough to justify the extra work.
claims.measure: Known-defect detection rate under planted defects (fake citation, skipped authorization, omitted failed attempt, changed denominator, dropped promise), plus JOINT false-acceptance rate across the producer/verifier pair on the same planted set, plus a clean-case control an indiscriminate rejecter would fail. 06 section 7 requires the joint measurement before agreement counts as assurance.
claims.existing_evidence: For the rule: 06 section 6 ('the producer may supply self-checks ... but cannot become sole independent acceptor by changing role labels'; 'an always-pass reviewer must fail the known-defect control'). Against inferring independence from separation: research/L04-engineering.md ('a separate invocation alone cannot establish that independence'); 02-architecture-selection.md section 5 ('two models consuming the same bad parser do not supply that independence')
claims.model_generation_note: Correlated error between producer and verifier is a property of the shared model and is the quantity that decides whether separation buys anything.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F4 independent verification

claims.statement: A set of persistent agents without shared state produces worse accepted outcomes, or more owner labour, than the same capabilities coordinated around one shared source of truth.
claims.measure: Matched fixtures under both arrangements with identical external obligations, information, total resources and owner allowance (the EAS-R1 comparison discipline frozen in 02 section 9); accepted outcomes, omitted duties and founder translation minutes reported separately, no aggregate score.
claims.existing_evidence: none in package as a comparison; research/L03-architectures.md declines to license the converse - 'the evidence does not justify these extrapolations: more agents necessarily improve outcomes ... role titles establish authority or evaluation independence'
claims.model_generation_note: A claim about where state lives, which is an architecture property.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F6 founder absent

claims.statement: Executors reading one authoritative view of goals, current decisions, canonical files, verified knowledge and next actions produce fewer contradictory or duplicated actions than executors reading their own assembled context.
claims.measure: Count of contradictory actions, duplicated external effects and actions taken against a superseded decision, per fixture run, against a baseline where each executor assembles its own context from the same underlying records.
claims.existing_evidence: none in package as a measured comparison. Mechanisms exist in specification: 06 section 1 assigns six memory jobs to distinct representations; 05 section 4 deliberately NARROWS the thesis - 'workers can read authorized peers' work projections; they cannot see all company context merely to coordinate'
claims.model_generation_note: Where state lives and who may write it is an architecture property, not a model capability.
claims.discriminating_fixture: New - two executors, one superseded decision: the founder changes a decision mid-run; measure actions taken against the old one and the length of the stale window under each arrangement

claims.statement: Goals, current decisions, canonical files, verified knowledge and an updated view of what should happen next are together sufficient as the shared source of truth for whole-company work.
claims.measure: Coverage test against the 46 requirements in coverage/capability-requirements.json: for each, name the constituent carrying what an executor must know to act. Anything landing nowhere is a missing constituent; test surviving obligations, active restrictions and deletion scopes, current grants, counterparty standing and capacity state first.
claims.existing_evidence: Against sufficiency, implicitly: 02 section 3 treats surviving obligations as outliving the case carrying them, and section 4 treats grants, holds and restriction epochs as separately owned state
claims.model_generation_note: Whether a list of constituents covers the work is a coverage question; no model change adds a missing constituent.
claims.discriminating_fixture: New - the closed case with a live duty: close a case whose refund duty survives it, then ask each constituent where that duty is now visible

claims.statement: A substantial share of published multi-agent frameworks decompose work by human role name rather than by tools, permissions, context or verification need.
claims.measure: Descriptive, already satisfied for the inspected set; R3 extends the census and records, per system, whether the role names carry any enforced difference in tools, permissions or context.
claims.existing_evidence: research/L03-architectures.md (MetaGPT's product-manager/architect/engineer assembly line; CrewAI's role backstories and manager hierarchies; CAMEL's role-playing failures: role reversal, repeated instructions, promises without execution); CLAUDE.md (this repository's harness began with 21 named roles, ten with no agent file and eleven routing shims)
claims.model_generation_note: A descriptive census of how published systems are organized; the organization does not change when the model does.
claims.discriminating_fixture: Not applicable - descriptive claim settled by census, not by fixture

claims.statement: Decomposing by human job title produces worse accepted outcomes, or more coordination cost, than decomposing by work, authority, tools, skills and context.
claims.measure: Same fixtures, two decompositions, MATCHED executor count and matched total capacity; accepted outcomes, handoff losses (TC-01's probe) and coordination minutes reported separately. Matching executor count is what stops this becoming a re-run of TC-20.
claims.existing_evidence: For: CLAUDE.md - the 21-role roster collapsed to seven engines with zero resolving to a real engine directly, which HANDOFF-F2 section 2 flags as evidence about one harness, not a law. Against inferring more: research/L03-architectures.md preserves the competing organization interpretation ('human roles package useful expertise ... roles may carry irrelevant social structure') and declines to resolve it
claims.model_generation_note: A stronger general model may make role scaffolding redundant (L04's ablation lesson), but the coordination cost of titles is not obviously a model property.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F1 unknown job - a job with no matching title forces a title-based decomposition to invent one or drop the work

claims.statement: Work, authority, tools, skills and context are separable axes - an executor can differ on one without differing on the others - and together they cover every difference that matters.
claims.measure: Separability: construct one real work item differing on each axis alone; an axis that cannot vary independently is not an axis. Coverage: express each needed difference across the 46 capability requirements in the five; anything left over is a sixth axis. Consequence class and counterparty standing are the likeliest leftovers.
claims.existing_evidence: 02 section 3 organizes by a different cut - deterministic computation, durable procedure, bounded model work, capable people, qualified professionals - a production-mode axis the founder's five do not contain
claims.model_generation_note: Separability and coverage of the axes are structural properties of the taxonomy.
claims.discriminating_fixture: New - the same work at two consequence classes: drafting an internal note versus drafting an outward customer promise, identical in work, tools, skills and context

claims.statement: During ordinary operation, kinds of work that no one specified in advance arrive often enough that handling them is a primary design requirement, not an edge case.
claims.measure: Over a fixed operating window, count admitted work items whose kind matches no existing capability contract, procedure or skill, as a fraction of all admitted items; record disposition as absorbed, escalated or dropped.
claims.existing_evidence: 02 section 8 retains adaptive cases specifically for unfamiliar work, citing L13's CMMN reading; research/L13-contrarian.md records that CMMN complements predefined processes with case work depending on evolving circumstances. That supports the mechanism's existence, not the rate. The founder's own report is testimony about his experience.
claims.model_generation_note: A property of running a company, not of the model.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F1 unknown job

claims.statement: A new kind of work can be admitted, typed, staffed and accepted without a person editing a capability catalog, a routing table or an agent definition.
claims.measure: Run F1 and count HUMAN EDITS TO SYSTEM DEFINITIONS required before the work reaches accepted (capability contracts, routing rules, skills, templates, schemas). Zero edits with a correct accepted outcome supports it. Separately count silent mistyping into the nearest existing kind, which is worse than an honest refusal and must not be scored as success.
claims.existing_evidence: Partly specified, untested: 05 section 2 ('Unfamiliar work starts with a bounded discriminator before a large commitment'); 05 section 4 gives the role-gap symptoms and routes the response through the maintenance custodian proposing and the legitimate capability owner approving - a human in the loop, so the package as written does not currently claim TC-19
claims.model_generation_note: Typing unfamiliar work is an interpretation task.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F1 unknown job, run once with the founder available and once under F6 founder absent

claims.statement: Beyond some number, adding executors within one domain raises capacity per accepted outcome and lowers context quality, with no compensating gain.
claims.measure: Sweep executor count within one domain at fixed total capacity (1, 3, 7, 15, 30), reporting accepted outcomes, capacity per accepted outcome, handoff losses and coordination minutes at each point. The claim predicts a turning point; the measurement's job is to find whether one exists and where.
claims.existing_evidence: research/L13-contrarian.md reads Coase as comparing costly internal coordination against costly market transactions, inferring that coordination and assurance costs may dominate - a reason to expect a turning point, not a measurement of one
claims.model_generation_note: Per-executor cost moves with the generation and the turning point moves with it.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F2 demand 4x

claims.statement: One undifferentiated executor with all tools and all context cannot deliver the whole-company scope at acceptable safety and cost.
claims.measure: Run the S0-style single-executor arm on the full fixture set holding the union of permissions and record where it fails: released operations outside scope, disclosure count, accepted-outcome rate, capacity per outcome.
claims.existing_evidence: 02 section 2 keeps S0 as a serious operating comparator; 02 section 9 commits to reducing the system if manual/native coordination delivers equivalent useful outcomes and recovery within the same owner allowance at lower full cost; 05 section 9 repeats the obligation
claims.model_generation_note: Precisely the claim a much stronger model could overturn.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F3 three permissions, with the single executor holding all three

claims.statement: For this system's scope, some multi-executor arrangement beats the best single-executor arrangement on accepted outcomes at matched capacity.
claims.measure: Best-of-each comparison at matched total capacity across the full fixture set, with owner minutes and unauthorized consequences reported separately and never summed.
claims.existing_evidence: Against: research/L03-architectures.md ('the evidence does not justify ... more agents necessarily improve outcomes'), and MAST's failure taxonomy is drawn entirely from multi-agent traces. For: the same lane's useful mechanisms - bounded delegation, typed handoffs, separate thread state, replaceable workers - and 02 section 3's retention of specialized production. The lane's verdict is that these do not justify resolving into one universal pattern
claims.model_generation_note: Both arms move with the generation, and every comparison cited here was run on older models than the ones this system would use.
claims.discriminating_fixture: The whole fixture set; no single case decides it

claims.statement: Whether a capability is deterministic software, a fixed workflow, an LLM-assisted workflow, a temporary agent, a persistent agent, a group, a human or an external professional is chosen by the nature of the work, never to maximize agent count.
claims.measure: Conformance, not effect: every proposed executor in a candidate model must name the property of the work that put it in that mode.
claims.existing_evidence: inputs/DIRECTIVE.md section 1.2 ('Choose based on the nature of the work rather than the desire to maximize the number of agents'; 'Do not begin by inventing agent names and roles'); implemented as the five-way production rule in 02 section 3; registers/decisions.json AD-002
claims.model_generation_note: A directive constraint on how a mode is chosen; it binds whatever the model can do.
claims.discriminating_fixture: Applies to every fixture as an admissibility check on candidate models

claims.statement: A created executor holds an attenuated subset of its creator's authority, and no executor can increase its own authority.
claims.measure: Attempt the escalation on a live fixture and observe refusal at the enforcement boundary rather than in instruction text; count operations released, not attempted.
claims.existing_evidence: inputs/DIRECTIVE.md section 8.16 ('No agent may grant itself greater authority. No component may silently inherit all permissions of the process that created it'); 05 sections 1 and 5; 02 section 4 ('A model can propose another step but cannot admit its own larger mandate')
claims.model_generation_note: Attenuation is enforced outside the model; a more capable model does not loosen or tighten it.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F3 three permissions, with a delegation attempt that asks for a fourth

claims.statement: The supervision an action requires is set by its possible consequence, reversibility and blast radius; a good record may change review depth but may not silently raise the owner's maximum exposure.
claims.measure: Monotonic-exposure check across a long run: an executor's accumulated record must not move any action into a lower supervision class.
claims.existing_evidence: inputs/DIRECTIVE.md section 1.5; 05 section 4 ('Trust is scoped eligibility, not a general score ... Success never expands authority automatically')
claims.model_generation_note: Supervision is set by consequence, which is a property of the action and not of the executor's model.
claims.discriminating_fixture: New - the well-behaved executor: run one executor to a long clean record, then check that the set of actions it may take without approval is identical to its first hour

claims.statement: Internal execution economics are measured in subscription allowance, provider quota buckets, concurrency and owner attention, tracked separately; no silent fallback to a metered path is permitted.
claims.measure: Any cost comparison in this round reporting dollars per token as its primary unit is non-conforming and must be re-reported in the units of 07 section 6. This constraint binds TC-02's measure directly.
claims.existing_evidence: inputs/DIRECTIVE.md section 8.21; 07-integrations-capacity.md section 6; registers/decisions.json AD-007
claims.model_generation_note: The unit of account is fixed by the directive; only the values measured in it move with the generation.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F2 demand 4x, where the subscription ceiling binds and a token price would not have predicted it

claims.statement: Each significant run records what context was loaded, why, from where, its version, age and trust level, what was omitted, what was summarized and what may have been lost.
claims.measure: Conformance plus a falsification probe: the manifest is produced by the server that delivered the inputs, and a run whose manifest disagrees with its actual delivered inputs must be detectable.
claims.existing_evidence: inputs/DIRECTIVE.md section 8.12; 06 section 2 ('the server discovers and records actual delivered inputs. The caller's claimed read list is not trusted'). This is the instrument TC-01 and TC-04 depend on; without it they have nothing to measure
claims.model_generation_note: The manifest requirement is a record-keeping obligation; what it records changes, the obligation does not.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F5 capacity reset

claims.statement: Selection quality and selection cost must not worsen as the skill library grows.
claims.measure: Hold the relevant question set fixed and grow the library to 10, 100 and 1000 packages with adversarial near-duplicates; report selection time, candidates inspected, bytes loaded, wrong selections and accepted outcomes at each size.
claims.existing_evidence: inputs/DIRECTIVE.md section 8.9 ('Prevent an expanding skill library from making selection progressively worse'); 05 section 8 specifies exactly this test and labels the sizes UNKNOWN - 'These are test sizes, not proven capacity'
claims.model_generation_note: Selection is an interpretation task, so the degradation curve moves with the model even though the requirement does not.
claims.discriminating_fixture: The 10/100/1000 library sweep specified in 05 section 8

claims.statement: The system deliberately returns selected work, evidence, customer material and decisions to the founder even when it could process them automatically, as a designed mechanism rather than a recommendation.
claims.measure: Delayed unfamiliar-transfer test: after an absence, measure recognition and intervention performance on material the founder did not see being produced. Attendance, confidence and agreement with the model are explicitly not competence.
claims.existing_evidence: inputs/DIRECTIVE.md section 1.6 ('This must be a designed mechanism, not an optional recommendation'); 06 section 6 attention/competence row; 02 section 7; registers/decisions.json AD-006; research/cross-lane-comparison.json X07 records that no founder-specific dose is validated
claims.model_generation_note: A better model could process more on the founder's behalf, which makes the constraint bind harder rather than less.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F6 founder absent

claims.statement: No executor exists because a human company has that department.
claims.measure: Conformance check on every candidate model: for each proposed executor, name the engineering difference that justifies it. Section 8.8 forbids the imitation and explicitly leaves open whether human structures are useful, so this constraint does not settle TC-16.
claims.existing_evidence: inputs/DIRECTIVE.md section 8.8 ('Do not create agents merely to imitate human departments'); 02 section 3 ('Existing roster names do not supply that justification'); 02 section 6 (the 46 capabilities are 'required capabilities, not future departments')
claims.model_generation_note: A prohibition on a reason for creating an executor; no model change makes departmental imitation a reason.
claims.discriminating_fixture: Applies to every candidate as an admissibility check

claims.statement: It is not established whether one shared source of truth means one store, one schema, one authority over many native stores, or a contract that native systems satisfy.
claims.measure: Enumerate the candidate readings, then test each against a case where an accounting system, a CRM and a support tool each hold a different current answer about the same customer; the surviving reading says which answer is authoritative and who may change it.
claims.existing_evidence: 02 section 5 answers a narrower question - 'Native accounting, CRM, support, code, design and professional meanings remain authoritative in their domains. Shared meaning covers only actual cross-boundary decisions' - closer to the fourth reading than the first, and never checked against the thesis wording
claims.model_generation_note: A definitional question about where authority over a fact sits; no model change answers it.
claims.discriminating_fixture: New - three systems, one customer, three answers: a ticket closed, an invoice unpaid and a CRM stage of won, all current, all disagreeing

claims.statement: The thesis makes context engineering the central variable and supplies no measure for it.
claims.measure: Propose and test candidate metrics - facts-present rate, facts-used rate (decision probe), load-bearing-fact loss per transformation, manifest completeness, stale-fact use rate. A metric qualifies only if it moves when context quality is deliberately degraded and does not move under a sham change.
claims.existing_evidence: 06 section 2 supplies the instruments (ContextTransformation, SummaryLoss, deterministic exact-field comparison, independent semantic challenge) without naming a headline metric; research/L05-memory.md warns that calling retention, retrieval, applicability, provenance, authorization and omission all 'memory' risks hiding failures behind successful recall
claims.model_generation_note: The metric should be model-independent even though its value is not.
claims.discriminating_fixture: New - the sham context change: a rewording preserving every load-bearing fact must not move the metric; deleting one exclusion must move it

claims.statement: The thesis lists specialized knowledge as a reason an agent earns existence; the package treats know-how as a versioned skill loaded by a general executor. Which unit carries specialization is undecided.
claims.measure: For a fixed domain competence, build both and compare on the same outcome criteria, including maintenance cost and what happens when the domain changes underneath each.
claims.existing_evidence: 05 section 8 ('SkillVersion is a reusable procedure package, not a new agent'). The founder's sentence and that sentence cannot both be the design
claims.model_generation_note: The stronger the general model, the less a specialist unit buys over a loaded skill, so the answer can flip between generations.
claims.discriminating_fixture: New - the domain that changes: a rule the domain depends on changes; compare what must be edited, retested and revalidated under each unit

claims.statement: The thesis requires a current view of next actions and does not say who produces it, whether it binds anyone, or what happens when it is wrong.
claims.measure: For each candidate answer - the case authority, each executor locally, a planner, a derived projection - test whether an executor can act against it, whether it can be stale, and whether being wrong is detectable before the action releases.
claims.existing_evidence: 02 section 4 gives the scheduler that function under endorsed priorities; 05 section 3 makes C02 the only advancer of a workflow cursor. The package has an answer and the thesis's phrasing is broader than it
claims.model_generation_note: Authorship of and authority over a next-action view are design choices, not model capabilities.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F6 founder absent - a next-action view is only load-bearing when nobody is watching it

claims.statement: The founder writes 'such as' and then lists five criteria; whether the list is closed decides whether a sixth reason may create an executor.
claims.measure: R2 returns the strongest candidate sixth reasons with evidence; whether the list is closed is then a founder decision packet, not a research finding.
claims.existing_evidence: inputs/FOUNDER-THESIS-2026-09-13-agents.md - 'such as parallel work, distinct tools or permissions, isolated context, specialized knowledge, or independent verification'
claims.model_generation_note: A question about the founder's intended scope for his own list.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F3 three permissions plus the consequence-class fixture from TC-17, which between them produce the two strongest sixth-reason candidates

claims.statement: It is not established whether the thing that must justify its existence is a template, a running instance, a standing role, a context boundary or a permission scope.
claims.measure: Apply the five criteria to each candidate unit and see which produces a decidable answer; a criterion that cannot be evaluated against a unit is evidence that unit is the wrong one.
claims.existing_evidence: 05 section 4 already separates them - AgentTemplate is 'a versioned production recipe ... not an identity with standing', AgentInstance binds one recipe to one admitted WorkOrder - so the package has three units where the thesis has one word
claims.model_generation_note: A definitional question about the unit of justification; it is the same question for any model.
claims.discriminating_fixture: Not a scenario - a definitional resolution R2 must return before its other findings can be read

claims.statement: Whether independent verification is achievable when producer and verifier share a model family is unresolved.
claims.measure: Joint false-acceptance rate on controlled planted defects across same-family producer/verifier pairs, against the cheapest non-model discriminators: a deterministic counterexample, actual destination state, original customer evidence, a scoped professional assessment.
claims.existing_evidence: 06 section 7 ('A different model family can add a tested viewpoint but is not a proof of independent error ... Measure joint false acceptance on controlled defects before treating panel agreement as extra assurance'); CLAUDE.md records single-family review as an accepted risk with an exit condition; HANDOFF-F2 section 0 line 20 requires that procedural independence is stated and never laundered
claims.model_generation_note: Correlated error is a property of the shared model.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F4 independent verification

claims.statement: The five criteria are written about agents; whether they also govern when a human, a professional or an external service should be a distinct performer is unaddressed.
claims.measure: Apply each criterion to a case requiring an actual professional determination and see whether it yields the right answer. Specialized knowledge and independent verification plausibly do; isolated context and parallel work plausibly do not.
claims.existing_evidence: 02 section 3 puts capable people and qualified professionals in the same production rule as models, so the package applies one rule where the thesis speaks only about agents
claims.model_generation_note: Whether the criteria govern human and professional performers is a scope question about the thesis, not about capability.
claims.discriminating_fixture: New - the filing that is not a filing: preparing a professional packet is preparatory work and sending it is not filing (02 section 1); which criterion tells you a separate performer is required?

claims.statement: The thesis's costs are asserted without a scale; it is unknown whether they bind at three executors, thirty, or only above some throughput.
claims.measure: The TC-20 sweep, reporting the threshold as the finding rather than the direction, separately for executor count, concurrency and total work admitted per period, because these can have different thresholds.
claims.existing_evidence: 07 section 6 fixes concurrency at CP1 = one native job plus one external job, so at currently admitted capacity most of the thesis's costs cannot arise - the package's current concurrency makes several thesis claims untestable as specified
claims.model_generation_note: The threshold moves with per-executor cost and with how much one context can hold, both generation properties.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F2 demand 4x, the only fixture that moves the scale

claims.statement: TC-19 requires the system to recognise unanticipated work; the recogniser, its evidence and its failure modes are unspecified.
claims.measure: Confusion matrix on a labelled stream containing familiar work, genuinely new kinds, and familiar work in unfamiliar wording. Silent mistyping into the nearest existing kind is the failure to hunt and must be separated from an honest refusal to type.
claims.existing_evidence: 05 section 4 gives the symptoms of a role gap and routes the response through human approval; 05 section 10 registers SkillSelection.no_match as distinct from budget_exhausted - 'the difference is whether the search finished' - which is the right shape for this problem one level up
claims.model_generation_note: Recognising an unfamiliar kind of work is an interpretation task, so the confusion matrix moves with the model.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F1 unknown job, with familiar-work-in-unfamiliar-wording decoys included

claims.statement: The thesis rejects disconnected employees in favour of coordinated capabilities without saying whether coordination is a component, a shared record or an emergent property - or, if a component, what justifies its own existence under the five criteria.
claims.measure: Build the fixture under each reading - explicit coordinator, shared record with no coordinator, executors negotiating pairwise - and measure contradictory actions, duplicated effects and owner minutes.
claims.existing_evidence: 02 section 3 selects an explicit coordinator (the case admission authority); 02 section 2 names its cost as concentrated agenda authority; 02 section 9 commits to reopening if that concentration misses important work, increases owner labor or obstructs independently capable domains
claims.model_generation_note: Whether coordination is a component, a record or emergent is an architecture choice.
claims.discriminating_fixture: F1 unknown job under F6 founder absent - the case with no obvious owner is where a coordinator either earns its keep or does not

claims.statement: The thesis makes one shared truth the foundation and does not say how a false entry is detected, corrected, or prevented from propagating to every executor that trusts it.
claims.measure: Plant a false entry - a superseded price, a closed duty that is still live, a corrected fact - and measure blast radius: how many executors acted on it, time to detection, whether the correction reached dependent work, and whether the older decision's context is still reconstructable afterwards.
claims.existing_evidence: 06 section 4 requires a correction to be checked by 'a new bounded case or a direct critical-field check' because 'storing the correction alone is insufficient'; 06 section 3 keeps a ContradictionSet rather than forcing a winner; research/L05-memory.md reports Memora finding recurring invalid-memory reuse across four models and six memory agents, so the failure is observed rather than hypothetical
claims.model_generation_note: Whether a corrected fact actually displaces the superseded one in behaviour is a model property, and Memora measured it.
claims.discriminating_fixture: New - the correction that must bite: the founder corrects a fact mid-run; count actions taken on the old value after the correction is recorded
